brief:
Macklemore was removed from Ed Sheeran's tour after calling for Palestinian freedom, according to Mondoweiss, which attributed the decision to pressure from New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft. The outlet reports the incident illustrates how the entertainment industry enforces political silence on Palestinian rights while permitting other forms of political speech.

Critics argue the removal reflects what Mondoweiss characterizes as the industry's historical pattern of suppressing voices addressing racial injustice and colonialism. The outlet draws parallels to Billie Holiday's 1930s performance of "Strange Fruit," a protest song about lynching, suggesting contemporary suppression of Palestine advocacy follows the same logic of selective censorship based on whose lives and suffering the industry chooses to amplify.
dek: How Robert Kraft got Macklemore booted from Ed Sheeran's tour for saying "Free Palestine" — and why the backlash reveals the racial logic of "neutrality," from Billie Holiday's "Strange Fruit" to today's entertainment industry.
title: Music industry silences Palestine advocacy, critics say
